strings.title: THE_TIMEKEEPER
strings.subtitle: Problem: not disclosed. Read the data.
strings.briefing:
Meeting rooms are booked in blocks of time, and bookings in the same room often overlap or run back to back. Facilities wants to know when each room is actually occupied, as continuous blocks.

Merge the bookings of each room. Two bookings belong to the same block when they overlap, or when one starts at exactly the moment another ends (back to back). A booking can lie entirely inside another, and a long booking can swallow several short ones. Rows come in no particular order.

Give one row per merged block: room, block_start, block_end, bookings (how many bookings the block contains). Times are written like 2026-04-14 09:30.

In Python, put your answer in df (df = ...); that table is what gets judged.

In SQL, create a NEW table named result that holds your answer: CREATE TABLE result AS SELECT ...; That table is what gets judged. You can run your query as often as you like; each run replaces the old result.
strings.task: Merge each room's overlapping or touching bookings into continuous blocks. Columns: room, block_start, block_end, bookings.
